review.title: the review page
redlines: The design laid the panel beside a plain card; the build lays both on a ruled, tilted desk (panel.desk) and scales the frame to fit, with the zoom read out in the corner (panel.zoom).

The design's tabs were Blueprints / Rules / Screens. Built: Blueprints / Rules / Threads with counts, and the screens moved into the bar as a picker (panel.screen-picker) that names the page in the frame.

Rules are grouped under the screen they are about, with a sticky screen head, tier marks on the left and the ask — sign / asks / fixed / walk — as a coloured badge on the right (ADR 0006 §4). The design had story headings and one sign / walk word.
The bar carries Start walkdown, the viewport presets and Pin mode; Recording as moved to the settings pop-over under the gear.
The footer counts verified rules and opens the Legend on demand; the design printed the legend inline.

rule-detail.title: rule detail
redlines: The design had a verdict block at the top — a why box, Pass and Fail — and a separate Threads list with its own composer at the bottom. Built: one conversation, one composer under it (ADR 0006): the text box above the buttons, Waive alone on the left, Reply / Fail / Pass on the right.
The statement is followed by because and history, then the screen and the steps drawn as given / when / then with anchors as chips (ADR 0004). The design showed statement, evidence, steps, verify.
Evidence, acceptance and the check source sit below the conversation rather than above it.
The steppers (← →) and ← All rules are where the design put them.
The conversation shows only the last thing said; the whole history is one slide to the right, behind History (n-0319). The design showed every thread in place.

thread-panel.title: the thread screen
redlines: The design's composer offered Answer and Waive under the box. Built: the box, then Reply — and on a thread that has ended, the closed banner above it says how it ended and that a fail on the rule reopens it (ADR 0006 §3). Done / Reopen appear only on a thread no walkable rule owns.
The head names the author, the id and the reason (finding, feedback, request…) beside the status chip; the design had id and status alone.
This screen is reached from the Threads tab — which lists only threads no rule can be walked — or from a tag in a rule's conversation. The design reached it from a rule's Threads list.
Day dividers and the NEW line are as designed.
An open question's screen carries its choices under the question, with Answer and Later at the foot, so it is answered here as well as on the rule (n-0319).

settings.title: settings
redlines: The design drew a card: Record as, then the desk ruling. Built as a pop-over under the gear in the bar, over the page, with the actor's username, full name, timezone and roles read from ~/.walkdown/config.yml and said so.
Record as is the username the records carry; the full name is only how you are shown. The design had one box.
The desk ruling — tilt, tip, depth, spacing, ink, hide — is as designed, with Reset.

start.title: first run
redlines: As designed: a first step, not an error. The build explains why a server is needed (a browser tab cannot read the filesystem) before naming walkdown serve; the design said it in one line.
The server box and Connect are the Blueprints tab's own row, drawn here too (n-0236).

project-modal.title: which project?
redlines: Built from the proposal that was promoted on 2026-09-10 (n-0271): the modal covers the whole chrome, panel included, and the board behind it is blurred.
The address is named, then what is true of it (no blueprint claims it), then the two commands — walkdown claims and walkdown import — then every project this machine has, with its blueprint count.
This one screen also answers several projects claim this page and no page to route from (ADR 0001 §7); the retired unclaimed-page drawing was one of the three it folded.

choose-blueprint.title: choose a blueprint
redlines: The gate itself only rises when a project holds several blueprints and none is picked; this machine holds one per project, so what is drawn is the Blueprints tab, which lists the same rows with the same anchors (start.folder, start.options).

The design asked which blueprint is this site? with radio marks and a description per row. Built: the server row above, the folder named, and each blueprint as a row with its description — the one the page claims first.
Nothing is remembered for the site (ADR 0001 §9); the address carries the pick instead.
